transcription: Been denied promotion three times. Should I leave? For references I work at a golf course that has multiple courses at this location. I also have a bachelor's degree in golf course management. I work on the outside service team so we help people with their bags and getting their round started. I've been doing this for almost two years. I first got denied the promotion because when the spot opened up I was on a small vacation and I did not get my name in soon enough. Oh well it happens, and there was someone that was already in line to get it. I like that person so I'm not upset about that at all. Afterwards I asked what can I do to be next in line. I was told in short be a better leader, work harder and wait. So I did. I earned the respect of the rest of the service team. I would work sometimes six days a week. I also became the trainer of the service team. Those of you who work at a golf course know that those morning shifts are early like 4am early. The next time I was told it was between me and one other person. They gave it to the other person because they had pro shop experience. I had tried to work in the pro shop multiple times and it always got shut down. So I didn't get the spot because I was not let to work in the pro shop. The managers at this course mainly help out outside though. So almost the whole service team was mad or upset for me. I found out through someone that works in the pro shop still that they were told they didn't get the spot because they didn't have outside service experience. So the real reason we didn't get it is we did not kiss ass enough. So I asked again what can I do. I was told try to get pro shop experience, work harder and get into the PGA program. So I was pretty much told my degree means nothing. Also I was told to put myself out there more and stop flying under the radar. So don't let my actions do the talking.
